:::{#thm-newton-linearized-gradient}
#### The Newton step is the root of the linear approximation of the gradient

Let $f$, $\vx$, $\vecf{g}$ and the [Hessian](vector-calculus.qmd#def-hessian) $\matr{H}$ be as in @lem-gradient-linear-approximation,
with $\matr{H}$ [invertible](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-inverse).
The only step $\stepvec$ at which the [linear approximation of the gradient](#def-gradient-linear-approximation) is zero
is the [Newton step](#def-newton-step):

$$
\vecf{\ell}(\stepvec) = \vzero_{p \times 1}
\iff
\stepvec = -\matr{H}^{-1} \vecf{g}.
$$ {#eq-newton-linearized-gradient}

:::

::: proof

By @lem-gradient-linear-approximation,
$\vecf{\ell}(\stepvec) = \vzero_{p \times 1}$ exactly when

$$
\ba
\vzero_{p \times 1} &= \vecf{g} + \matr{H} \stepvec
&& \text{(@eq-gradient-linear-approximation-hessian)}
\\
-\vecf{g} &= \matr{H} \stepvec
&& \text{(subtract } \vecf{g} \text{ from both sides)}
\\
-\matr{H}^{-1} \vecf{g} &= \stepvec.
&& \text{(multiply both sides by } \matr{H}^{-1} \text{ on the left)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-newton-linearized-gradient-solve}

Each line implies the next and, because $\matr{H}$ is [invertible](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-inverse), the one before,
so $\stepvec = -\matr{H}^{-1} \vecf{g}$ is the only solution.

:::
